descriptionChirho: The ordinal number 'tenth' used to designate position in a sequence — the tenth day, month, or year in calendrical and genealogical contexts. Arabic 'الْعَاشِرِ' (al-ʿāshiri, the tenth), Korean '열째/열 번째' (yeoljjae/yeol-beonjjae, tenth), Spanish 'el décimo/décima' (the tenth), Hindi 'दसवें/दसवीं' (dasvẽ/dasvī̃, tenth masc/fem), Swahili 'wa kumi/ya kumi' (of ten, i.e. tenth) — all express ordinal sequence rather than fraction across twenty-two occurrences.

A fractional quantity meaning one-tenth, used as a unit of dry measure (a tenth of an ephah) in sacrificial prescriptions. Arabic 'عُشْرَ' (ʿushr, a tenth), Korean '십분의 일' (sipbunui il, one-tenth), Spanish 'décima de' (a tenth of), Hindi 'दसवां हिस्सा' (dasvā̃ hissā, tenth part), Swahili 'sehemu ya kumi' (portion of ten, i.e. one-tenth) — all distinguish the fractional/proportional meaning from the ordinal across seven occurrences in Numbers and Ezekiel.
